diagnosis: The Dun at Hungerford is a chalk/groundwater-dominated catchment with very damped flow (observed Q ranges 0.16 to 2.6 mm/d). Calibration over 1971-1997 (DDS, NSE) gives NSE 0.70, KGE 0.85, PBIAS +3%. In a split-sample test (calibrated 1971-85, validated 1986-97), validation NSE was about 0.73, with a +14% volume bias. The water balance cannot close as given: observed runoff (~0.6 mm/d) is larger than P minus PET would allow, which points to groundwater export or precipitation overestimation. HBV has no loss term, so the optimiser uses the snow routine as a loss mechanism instead (TT ~4.6 °C, SFCF ~0.47, very fast melt). This removes part of the cold-season rain and is not a real snow process. A version with physically sensible snow parameters had a +16-21% volume bias and lower calibration NSE (0.53 vs 0.63-0.65 for the loss versions). Its validation NSE was similar (0.72 vs 0.73). Because the loss depends on temperature, a warmer future period could bring some overestimation. Other parameters: large FC (~600 mm) with LP ~0.55 to maximise ET, and a slow baseflow store (K2 ~0.021, K1 ~0.04, PERC ~3.6). Weaknesses: timing of individual peaks, multi-year groundwater memory (droughts and recessions) and volume bias. I am fairly confident in the response parameters but not in the snow and soil parameters, which mainly act as a correction for the water balance.
